highlights: Not researching speakers, agenda, or topics leads to FOMO and confusion.
Going without a clear goal makes it easy to get lost during the event.
Skipping workshops and expos means missing key insights and networking.
Not following up loses valuable contacts and opportunities.
Ignoring your post-conference action plan wastes all your notes.

blocks.text: Before the Conference

This experience begins even before the event itself. You should spend some time preparing for the event. Try to research which speakers will be present and what they look like. Which topics would be the main ones as well? Let’s look at the most common mistakes during this phase and how to prepare for the conference.
Mistake #1 —  Being Late

Respect your time and the event organisers. Every delay is a loss of a unique experience that will never be repeated. Even 15 minutes late can deprive you of the opportunity to learn something new. To be on time, plan your itinerary in advance and always allow a little extra time.
Mistake #2 — Not Researching Speakers, Exhibitors, and Agenda in Advance

To stay up to date on everything happening at a wellness event, it’s essential to do your research. This approach will help you avoid FOMO, get into the flow of discussions quickly, and make new connections. To do this, simply check the keynote speakers and topics discussed when registering for the conference.

Mistake #3 — Going Without a Clear Purpose
If you don’t know what you’re doing at a biohacking conference, you won’t get the most out of it.

To avoid getting lost during the event, think about your primary goal. Define it and focus on it. For example, if you’re focused on [optimising your sleep](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/biohacking-sleep), don’t get distracted by nutrition. There’s always a wealth of information, so keep your goal in mind and know the purpose of the conference essentials for you.
Mistake #4 — Wearing “the Wrong” Outfit

Remember that any conference is a formal event. Therefore, it’s important to consider the dress code. Of course, don’t be overly formal unless the conference press release specifically calls for it. Smart casual is best; this style conveys a relaxed and confident demeanour.
During the Conference

So, we’ve completed the preparatory stage and are ready to go! It’s time to think about how to attend the conference. This is an exciting moment when you want to take lots of notes and remember everything. So we need to figure out what to do during the event itself. Let’s review what not to do at a conference.
Mistake #5 — Skipping the Expo and Workshops

We often think that workshops will be boring or require too much talking. But in fact, these are the very parts where you can really shine and make new connections. The Biohakers World Conference and EXPO offers just that opportunity. Here you can gain unique insights in sun-drenched Los Angeles. Here you can discover the entire biohacking conference community and expand your horizons.

Mistake #6 — Ignoring Unspoken Etiquette Rules

Conference etiquette is not just written in the press release before the event. It is important to understand some unwritten rules as well. Biohackers value their own space and try not to violate others’ boundaries. Avoid interrupting speakers or hogging the microphone, and keep your questions brief. Avoid intruding on personal conversations; only continue them if your interlocutor wants to talk.
Mistake #7 — Not Networking (or Doing It Wrong)

[Networking](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/how-to-network-at-biohacking-conferences) is a crucial part of the event. This is where you can get the most out of the conference. Respect each fellow attendee’s thoughts, and you’ll gain biohacking essentials and insights you might not have expected. Try to feel the atmosphere of your chats, and if you notice it goes wrong, don’t push it, just thank the person and go to someone else.

blocks.text: Mistake #8 — Trying to Be Everywhere at Once

Trying to do everything is a desire of every biohacker, because we always work holistically and on our own bodies. But don’t rush around the conference trying to do everything. This way, you’re more likely to lose most of the information once you leave the event.
Try focusing on a few goals to improve overall health.

For example, start with understanding [metcon training](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/metcon-workouts) and maintaining [physical fitness](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/fitness-and-biohacking), and then explore various [supplements](https://www.biohackers.world/blog/best-biohacking-supplements), vibration massages, infrared saunas, and other ways to keep your fitness.
Mistake #9 — Ignoring Your Health

It’s easy to forget about your state at such events. It’s important to know what to bring to the conference. For example, don’t forget water. Hydration is crucial, especially in closed spaces with many people. Also, monitor your blood sugar levels. It’s best to bring healthy snacks like nuts and dried fruit. Be mindful and pay attention to your mental state. If you feel anxiety creeping up, get some fresh air and spend some time alone.
After the Conference

This time is as important as the event itself. Here, you can implement the entire conference checklist you created earlier. Dedicate a reasonable amount of time to this period and don’t neglect it. Only then will you get results from the event, not just pleasant memories of the time spent.
Mistake #10 — Not Following Up

At a conference, you always interact with a lot of people, don’t forget to remind them about yourself afterwards! This is a completely normal practice and shouldn’t be embarrassing. Send short follow-up messages throughout the week. Show that you value the contact, even if it’s just a simple “Thanks for the conversation, it was nice exchanging ideas about sleep and recovery!”
Mistake #11 — Not Following Your Biohacking Post-Conference Action Plan

During the event itself, you probably took notes for later. The issue occurs during post-conference time. We easily get lost in daily routines and don’t follow the plan created enthusiastically throughout the event. Try not to miss this rush and maintain disciplined action with the same conference mindset you had before. This is the only way to achieve real results.
Mistake # 12 — Don’t Explore the City

Most conferences take place in different countries. This is a nice opportunity for you to explore new places. You can have an exceptional experience that is just as important as the biohacking conference itself. So don’t take a flight on the same day the event ends. Have an extra day to reflect on everything you’ve learnt in the new city landscapes. This will not only give your mind a rest but also help you process all the information you’ve learned. You might even have the opportunity to connect with new acquaintances in an informal atmosphere.
Summary

Conference mistakes are more costly than you might think- they’re not wasted minutes, but rather lost ideas, connections, and opportunities. We figured out some conference tips that could help you navigate the event and present yourself as a professional.
To get the most out of it:

items: arrive early and prepare according to the program;
set a goal and focus on key topics;
maintain a balance between activity and rest;
